category_title: Overage 8th-grade students at risk of dropping out
minimal_context: The student is revising a survey on a laptop to print and distribute to fellow students to gather information for a documentary.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's review the survey you are revising on the laptop to print out and distribute to your fellow students.

STUDENT: (Moving desks closer together) I feel a lot of people will answer ‘yes’ to this one. You know why? Cause I have a LOT of friends like that.

TUTOR: How are you planning to handle the completed surveys?

STUDENT: We want to make sure students feel safe returning their surveys. We decided it would be better to put them in a shoe-box, put tape around it, and then decorate it to ensure security.

TUTOR: You need to rewrite some of these items. Questions like the ones about abortion are too probing and should be knocked off the survey.

STUDENT: No, you’re going too fast! You have to slow down, man. Don’t rush it. Sex questions you always leave for the end. You sugar-coat them at first. And then you crack them!

options.A: Provide a less frequent schedule of breaks intermittently while the student is revising the survey questions on the laptop.
options.B: Establish the working practices of the group through consensus by creating a student pledge, and thereafter consistently reinforce it during the sessions.
options.C: Enable the autocorrect and text prediction functions on the student's laptop to assist them while they are revising the survey questions.
options.D: Guide the student through generating lists of main and follow-up survey questions, critiquing the surveys, and using a journal to reflect on learning.
